extraction.name: FLEURS: Few-shot Leaming Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech
extraction.description: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna
extraction.inLanguage: 102 languages including en, fr, es, de, zh, ru, ar, hi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection started with the FLoRes-101 dataset. For each sentence in 102 languages, three recordings were collected by three different native speakers. These recordings were then evaluated by additional workers to assess if they corresponded to the input sentence.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: About 21.5% of the sentences are missing in the first version because none of the three recordings were validated.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw text data comes from the FLoRes-101 dataset, which contains sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages by human translators.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Recordings are kept as they are, from either quiet or noisy environments, without any data augmentations like SpecAugment, speed perturbation, or simulated reverberation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text sentences underwent NFC and FST normalization, lower-casing, and punctuation removal. Words were split into characters, with a specific token defined as word boundaries.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Recordings were evaluated by additional workers to assess whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Recordings were validated by workers; invalid ones were discarded, resulting in between zero and three valid recordings per sentence.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Between zero and three recordings per sentence
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Native speakers with a balanced sex ratio of at least 30/70% when possible.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to fill the gaps of missing sentences in future versions of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to enable speech technology in more languages, catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding, and build speech technologies for everyone.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: About 21.5% of the sentences are missing in the first version because none of the recordings were validated.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: ASR, Speech-to-Text and Speech-to-Speech Translation, Speech LangID, and Multilingual Speech-to-Speech and Speech-to-Text Retrieval.
